title: Redwood discovery — Nyx Payments: latency & throughput
summary: Discovery focused on Nyx's p95 latency targets, concurrency needs, streaming behavior and token/sec benchmarking. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for fraud-detection and realtime chat assistants. Agreed next steps: Redwood to run a benchmark with Nyx sample prompts, share pricing and SOC2 docs, schedule a deep-dive on VPC/private deployment requirements.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
security: SOC2 / SSO / KMS / audit logs
action_items: Jordan Lee: send tailored pricing + Dedicated capacity options (due 2026-10-14)
Priya N.: schedule technical deep-dive and request Nyx sample payloads for benchmark (due 2026-10-15)
Aisha Khan (Nyx): provide 2 weeks of representative prompts and concurrency profile (due 2026-10-16)
Jordan Lee: share SOC2 + security pack and network diagram for Redwood Private (due 2026-10-14)
next_steps: Redwood to run token/sec and latency benchmark using Nyx sample workload
Share pricing and Dedicated capacity SLAs
Schedule VPC/private deployment deep-dive with Nyx infra team
Follow up with SOC2 docs and audit log examples
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, Jordan from Redwood here, with Priya from our SE team. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Carlos (CTO): Carlos here, Aisha, Liam and Sofia joining too. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:12] Jordan: Great. Goal today is to understand latency and throughput needs — p95 targets, concurrency, streaming behavior — and figure out whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private makes sense. Priya will mostly drive the tech questions.
[00:20] Priya (SE): Hi all. Quick question to start: what are your immediate SLAs for inference? p95, tail latency, that kind of thing?
[00:28] Carlos: For fraud detection inline, we need p95 under 200ms end-to-end for short context prompts (~50-100 tokens). For the chat assistant, p95 can be up to 1s but we need steady concurrency ~500 concurrent users during peak.
[00:38] Aisha: To add, for background scoring batch jobs it's less strict but throughput matters — we want token/sec numbers so we can size Dedicated.
[00:47] Priya: Okay that helps. When you say p95 under 200ms, is that model generation only or include networking & client processing?
[00:52] Liam: That's end-to-end, so network and whatever client side we add, ideally keep model/server latency under ~120-140ms to have slack.
[01:00] Priya: Good. For hosted vs dedicated, typical tradeoff: Hosted gives fastest time-to-prod but multitenant variability can add jitter; Dedicated gives predictable tail. Private gives total control for compliance but has ops overhead.
[01:12] Sofia: We're leaning Dedicated if we can guarantee p95 at our concurrency and predictable billing.
[01:18] Jordan: Makes sense. Can you share expected request shape? Avg prompt tokens, max tokens returned, streaming vs non-streaming?
[01:24] Aisha: Avg prompt about 80 tokens, we sometimes stream responses for chat (incremental tokens) — streaming is important for UX. For scoring tasks we do non-streaming, 1-2k max tokens in rare cases.
[01:36] Priya: For streaming there are two latency components: initial token latency and token/sec throughput for the stream. For warm KV-cached prefix hits we can get very low first-token latency. If you rely on long contexts and KV misses latency rises.
[01:49] Carlos: We heard Redwood has prefix caching and batching — can you quantify expected p95 improvements?
[01:54] Priya: On typical chat workloads, with prefix/KV cache hit rates >80% you'll often see p95 initial token latency drop by 30-50% compared to cold runs. Batching increases throughput but trades off tail latency; our Dedicated offering supports configurable batching policies and strict tail SLOs.
[02:10] Liam: Token/sec numbers — what's realistic on a Dedicated instance?
[02:14] Priya: Depends on model size and quantization. For a 13B variant quantized to 4-bit on A100-class hardware you'll see roughly 150-300 tokens/sec per GPU for synchronous generation, higher with pipelined streaming. For 7B models it can be 300-700 tokens/sec. Those are rough numbers — we recommend running your workload for exact numbers.
[02:35] Aisha: For scoring, we need bulk throughput — say 200qps of short prompts for batch scoring, but can be spread across time. We need to size for peak though.
[02:44] Priya: Right, 200 QPS of 80-token prompts is about 16k tokens/sec. With 300 tokens/sec per GPU you'd need ~55 GPU-equivalents — but batching and continuous batching can increase effective utilization. Also caching helps: if many prompts share prefixes caching reduces compute.
[03:05] Jordan: That's where quantization and model selection come in — smaller models for scoring, larger for chat. We'll propose a mix in the benchmark.
[03:11] Carlos: What about p95 under sustained 500 concurrent chat users?
[03:16] Priya: Concurrency maps to QPS depending on session patterns. If 500 concurrent produce e.g. 200 QPS for streaming starts, Dedicated with autoscaling and burst capacity can keep p95 under target; key is warm model instances and keeping KV caches warm.
[03:30] Priya: Also note streaming reduces perceived latency because tokens start arriving quickly, even if full-complete latency is higher. So UX-wise initial RTT is very important.
[03:39] Sofia: How do you measure p95? We need transparent tracing so we can correlate token latencies to infra.
[03:44] Priya: Redwood Console exposes per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, per-token breakdown, and tracing hooks. We can send sample traces as part of the security pack.
[03:52] Carlos: Security — we'll need SOC2, SSO with SAML, audit logs, KMS integration. Also data residency for EU.
[03:59] Jordan: Yep — we have SOC2 Type II, SAML/SSO and KMS options in Private and Dedicated. Hosted supports customer-owned KMS for encryption at rest in higher tiers. We'll share docs.
[04:08] Liam: If we go Private (VPC), how much ops overhead? We need network diagrams and what Redwood manages vs we manage.
[04:14] Priya: Private gives you the control plane in your VPC; Redwood provides orchestrator and runtime but you manage networking and some infra. We'll include a runbook and network diagrams in the deep dive.
[04:22] Aisha: For benchmarking — what do you need from us?
[04:25] Priya: Representative prompt sets (2 weeks) and concurrency profile; sample payloads, attach telemetry preferences and desired models to test (we'll include 7B and 13B variants). We'll run token/sec and p95 measurements for hosted and dedicated configs.
[04:37] Carlos: Can Redwood simulate our exact concurrency (50% streaming, 50% non-streaming) and run a p95 breakdown across percentiles?
[04:44] Priya: Yes — we can run synthetic clients to replicate concurrency and streaming patterns. We'll produce a spreadsheet with token/sec, p50/p95/p99, and GPU utilization.
[04:53] Jordan: Pricing question — is Dedicated billed by reserved GPU hours? And burst capacity?
[04:58] Jordan (customer interruption, mislabelled): Sorry, I mean — Jordan from Redwood: Dedicated is reserved capacity plus burst; you can have baseline commit and pay for overage or configured burst pool. We'll include pricing scenarios.
[05:11] Sofia: Any differences in tail behavior between Hosted and Dedicated?
[05:15] Priya: Hosted can have noisy neighbor jitter but our routing and burst pools try to smooth it; Dedicated is much more predictable for p95 especially for heavy streaming workloads, since you control scaling and instance counts.
[05:26] Carlos: Latency SLOs — do you offer SLA-backed p95?
[05:29] Jordan: For Dedicated enterprise contracts we can include latency SLAs with credits; hosted has best-effort and published perf profiles.
[05:36] Aisha: We also need to know about function/tool calling and structured output — that can add a chunk of tokens and thus affect latency.
[05:42] Priya: Right — the model generating structured outputs can increase token count. We recommend instrumenting end-to-end and building regen strategies. Streaming helps UX if outputs are long.
[05:50] Liam: Any notes on kernel selection/quantization reliability? We run a lot of edge cases and need consistent quality.
[05:55] Priya: Our runtime selects kernels and quantization profiles per model and benchmark run. We'll include quality regression notes — Redwood Optimize will recommend when quantization reduces quality beyond threshold.
[06:05] Jordan: Could you give a quick example of a benchmark deliverable?
[06:08] Priya: We'll run your sample workload against hosted baseline, then Dedicated 2-GPU, 4-GPU, etc. We'll report p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost per 1M tokens, and recommendations (model family, quantization, batching).
[06:20] Carlos: Sounds good. One more operational question — cold starts: how much of an effect does spinning up new model instances have on p95?
[06:26] Priya: Cold starts can add several hundred ms up to seconds depending on weight stage, but with warm pools and pre-warm policies cold start impact is minimal. We'll show warm vs cold numbers.
[06:35] Aisha: Are there any network optimizations? We're in multi-cloud.
[06:39] Priya: We support regional routing, peering, and can colocate endpoints to reduce network hop. For Private you'll be running in your VPC which gives you local network latency.
[06:48] Carlos: Ok can we book the benchmark and do the deep-dive next week?
[06:52] Jordan: Yes — Priya will send calendar invite. We'll need sample prompts by Friday.
[06:56] Priya: Action items recap: I'll request samples and schedule deep dive; Jordan sends pricing and SOC2 pack. Carlos/Aisha will share prompts.
[07:04] Sofia: Minor transcription glitch: earlier you said KV-cash, it's KV cache.
[07:07] (laughter)
[07:10] Jordan: Noted. Any other questions?
[07:12] Liam: Curious about A/B rollout — do you support canary and automatic fallback to cheaper model?
[07:18] Priya: Yes — Rollouts in the Console support canary, A/B, and automatic fallback based on latency or error rates.
[07:24] Carlos: Perfect. Let's reconvene after samples. Thanks.
[07:27] Jordan: Thanks everyone, sending notes and next steps.
[07:30] End of call.
